q: Who proposed the Five Kingdom system of classification?
R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom classification in 1969 based on cell structure, thallus organisation, mode of nutrition/reproduction, and phylogenetic…
Aristotle classified animals into Enaima and Anaima based on:
Aristotle grouped animals with red blood as Enaima and those without as Anaima.
The Two Kingdom classification was proposed by:
Linnaeus (1753) proposed the Two Kingdom system: Plantae and Animalia.
Which of these was NOT a criterion used in the Five Kingdom classification?
Whittaker's criteria were cell structure, thallus organisation, mode of nutrition/reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships — not body colour.
Which kingdom includes only prokaryotic organisms?
The cell wall of bacteria is typically composed of:
Bacterial cell walls are made of peptidoglycan (a polysaccharide + amino acid complex).
The protein that makes up bacterial flagella is:
Bacterial flagella are composed of the protein flagellin, unlike eukaryotic flagella (tubulin).
Spiral bacteria are Spirillum; comma-shaped are Vibrio, rod-shaped are Bacillus, spherical are Coccus.
Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria mainly due to differences in their:
Archaebacteria have a distinct cell wall structure enabling survival in extreme habitats.
Methanogens live in marshy areas and in the guts of ruminants, producing methane (biogas).
Halophiles thrive in highly saline (salty) habitats.
Thermoacidophiles inhabit hot, acidic environments like hot springs.
Heterocysts are specialised cells in cyanobacteria responsible for:
Heterocysts are the site of atmospheric nitrogen fixation in cyanobacteria like Nostoc and Anabaena.
Salmonella typhi causes typhoid fever in humans.
Xanthomonas axonopodis causes citrus canker in crop plants.
Bacillus anthracis is the causative agent of:
Bacillus anthracis causes anthrax in cattle and other animals.
The main mode of asexual reproduction in bacteria is:
Bacteria reproduce asexually mainly by fission.
Transfer of DNA between two bacteria
Conjugation is a sexual-like process where DNA is transferred from one bacterium to another.
Protista includes unicellular eukaryotic organisms, primarily aquatic.
Flagella/cilia in Protista are made up of the protein:
Unlike bacterial flagellin, protist flagella/cilia are made of tubulin.
Diatomaceous earth is formed from the fossilised remains of:
Diatom cell walls are embedded with silica, making them indestructible and forming diatomaceous earth after fossilisation.
Diatoms are considered the chief producers of which ecosystem?
Diatoms are the chief 'producers' of the ocean.
Red tides in the sea are caused by rapid multiplication of:
Gonyaulax, a red dinoflagellate, multiplies rapidly causing red tides and releases toxins harmful to marine life.
Euglenoids possess a flexible protein-rich layer called the:
Euglenoids have a pellicle instead of a cell wall, making the body flexible.
The aggregation formed by slime moulds under favourable conditions is called:
Slime moulds form a plasmodium, an aggregation that grows and spreads under favourable conditions.
Which protozoan group moves using pseudopodia?
Amoeboid protozoans like Amoeba use false feet (pseudopodia) for movement and prey capture.
Entamoeba is responsible for which human disease?
Entamoeba is an internal parasite causing amoebic dysentery.
Which protozoan group has a gullet that opens to the outside?
Ciliated protozoans like Paramoecium have a gullet into which cilia sweep food-laden water.
Plasmodium, the causative agent of malaria, belongs to which protozoan group?
Plasmodium is a sporozoan with a spore-like infectious stage in its life cycle.
The thread-like structures making up the fungal body are called:
Hyphae are the long, slender, thread-like structures that form the fungal body.
A network of hyphae is known as:
A network of hyphae together is called the mycelium.
Coenocytic hyphae are continuous and multinucleate, lacking cross-walls (septa).
The fungal cell wall is mainly composed of:
Unlike plants (cellulose), fungal cell walls are made of chitin and polysaccharides.
The symbiotic association between fungi and plant roots is called:
Mycorrhiza is the symbiotic association between fungi and roots of higher plants.
The dikaryotic (n+n) stage is prominently seen in which two fungal classes?
The dikaryophase, where cells contain two distinct nuclei, is characteristic mainly of Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes.
Phycomycetes typically have mycelium that is:
Phycomycetes (algal fungi) have aseptate, coenocytic mycelium, e.g. Mucor, Rhizopus.
Ascospores are produced in sac-like structures called:
Ascomycetes produce sexual ascospores in sac-like asci arranged in ascocarps.
Penicillin, the 'wonder drug', is extracted from:
Penicillin is extracted from Penicillium notatum and P. chrysogenum.
In Basidiomycetes, karyogamy and meiosis in the basidium produce four basidiospores exogenously.
Puccinia, the causative agent of rust disease in plants, belongs to:
Puccinia (rust) is a Basidiomycete, along with Ustilago (smut) and Agaricus (mushroom).
Their sexual phase is absent or unknown
Deuteromycetes reproduce only by asexual conidia; once a sexual phase is discovered, the fungus is reclassified into Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.
Alternaria solani causes which plant disease?
Alternaria solani causes early blight of potato, while Phytophthora infestans causes late blight.
Phytophthora infestans causes late blight of potato — historically linked to the Irish potato famine.
Which of these is an insectivorous plant?
Dionaea (Venus flytrap) is an insectivorous plant showing partial heterotrophy.
Cuscuta is an example of a plant that is:
Cuscuta is a parasitic plant, an exception to the fully autotrophic nature of Plantae.
Animal cells, unlike plant cells, characteristically:
Animal cells lack a cell wall, unlike plant cells which have a cellulosic wall.
Animals typically store food reserves as:
Unlike plants (starch), animals store food reserves as glycogen or fat.
The term 'virus' (meaning venom/poisonous fluid) was coined by Pasteur.
M.W. Beijerinck (1898) named the infectious fluid from diseased plants as:
Beijerinck termed the infectious extract 'Contagium vivum fluidum' (infectious living fluid).
W.M. Stanley (1935) demonstrated that crystallised viruses were largely composed of:
Stanley crystallised viruses and showed the crystals contained largely proteins.
Viruses contain genetic material that is:
Either DNA or RNA, never both
Viral genetic material is either DNA or RNA, but never both together.
The protein coat surrounding viral nucleic acid is called the:
The capsid is the protein coat protecting the viral nucleic acid, made of subunits called capsomeres.
Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) contains which type of genetic material?
TMV, a plant virus, contains single-stranded RNA.
Bacteriophages typically contain which type of genetic material?
A fully assembled virus particle outside the host cell is called a:
A virion is the complete assembled virus (protein coat + nucleic acid) found outside a host.
Viroids differ from viruses mainly in that they:
Lack a protein coat and exist as free RNA
Viroids lack a protein coat, unlike viruses, and consist of free low molecular weight RNA.
Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by:
PSTVD (Potato spindle tuber viroid) causes spindle tuber disease in potato, transmitted by aphids.
Prions are infectious abnormally folded proteins causing neurological disease.
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (mad cow disease) is caused by:
BSE (mad cow disease) is caused by prions, with CJD as its human analogue.
The human disease analogous to mad cow disease is:
CJD is the human neurological disease analogous to BSE, both caused by prions.
A lichen is a symbiotic association between:
Lichens are formed by a symbiotic association between a fungus (mycobiont) and an alga (phycobiont).
In a lichen, the algal partner is called the:
The algal component of a lichen, which is autotrophic, is called the phycobiont.
In a lichen, the fungal partner is called the:
The fungal (heterotrophic) component of a lichen is called the mycobiont.
Lichens are considered good indicators of:
Lichens do not grow in polluted areas, making them reliable indicators of air pollution.
Fungal cell walls contain chitin, while green plant cell walls are made of:
This difference (chitin vs cellulose) was one key reason the two-kingdom system was found inadequate.
Which organism was placed under 'algae' in the two kingdom system despite being unicellular, unlike its multicellular counterpart Spirogyra?
Chlamydomonas (unicellular) and Spirogyra (multicellular) were both grouped under algae despite the difference in body organisation.
In the five kingdom system, which kingdom brought together Chlamydomonas and Paramoecium?
Kingdom Protista united unicellular eukaryotes previously split between the plant and animal kingdoms.
Which kingdom in the five kingdom system has a body organisation described as 'tissue/organ/organ system'?
Animalia shows the most complex body organisation: tissue/organ/organ system level.
Cyanobacteria contain chlorophyll a and are photosynthetic autotrophs, similar to green plants.
Diatoms and dinoflagellates are both classified under which kingdom?
Both diatoms (Chrysophytes) and dinoflagellates are classes within Kingdom Protista.
Which protist class is described as a 'connecting link between plants and animals'?
Euglenoids show both plant-like (photosynthesis) and animal-like (predation) traits, making them a connecting link.
Slime mould spores are dispersed mainly by:
Slime mould spores, protected by resistant true walls, are dispersed via air currents.
Which fungal class reproduces mainly by fragmentation, lacking asexual spores?
Basidiomycetes lack asexual spores; vegetative reproduction occurs mainly by fragmentation.
Morels and truffles, considered edible delicacies, belong to which fungal class?
Morels, buffles (bracket fungi relatives) and truffles are edible Ascomycetes.
Colletotrichum causes red rot of sugarcane, and belongs to the Deuteromycetes.
Both Fungi (saprophytic/parasitic) and Animalia (holozoic etc.) are heterotrophic kingdoms.
The presence of chitin in the cell wall is characteristic of which kingdom?
Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin and polysaccharides, unlike the cellulose walls of plants.
Which of these correctly lists organisms from Kingdom Monera to Kingdom Animalia in Whittaker's sequence?
Whittaker's five kingdoms are conventionally ordered: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia — reflecting increasing complexity.
Zoospores and aplanospores are asexual spore types found in which fungal class?
Phycomycetes reproduce asexually via motile zoospores or non-motile aplanospores.
Ascocarps are the fruiting bodies of which fungal class?
Ascomycetes bear their ascospores in asci arranged within fruiting bodies called ascocarps.
Basidiocarps are the fruiting bodies of which fungal class?
Basidiomycetes arrange their basidia (bearing basidiospores) within fruiting bodies called basidiocarps.
Aristotle classified plants using simple morphology into which three groups?
Aristotle grouped plants morphologically into trees, shrubs, and herbs.
Which classification criterion was ignored by the two kingdom system but included in the five kingdom system?
Mode of nutrition and cell structure
The five kingdom system added cell structure, mode of nutrition, and phylogenetic relationships as criteria, which the two kingdom system ignored.
Aristotle's classification of animals into Aquatic and Terrestrial was based on:
Aristotle also grouped animals by their habitat into aquatic and terrestrial forms.
The two kingdom system placed both bacteria and fungi under which kingdom?
Under the two kingdom system, bacteria and fungi were both grouped under Plantae, ignoring fundamental differences in cell structure and nutrition.
In the five kingdom system, which kingdom shows the simplest level of body organisation?
Monera, being prokaryotic and unicellular, shows the simplest cellular level of organisation.
Which kingdom in the five kingdom system contains members with both autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition?
Both Monera and Protista contain autotrophic and heterotrophic members, unlike Plantae (autotrophic) and Animalia/Fungi (heterotrophic).
Which of these bacterial shapes is described as comma-shaped?
Vibrio-shaped bacteria are comma-shaped, as seen in Vibrio cholerae.
Which bacterial nutrition type obtains energy by oxidising inorganic substances like nitrites?
Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidise inorganic substrates such as nitrites and ammonia to obtain energy.
The gelatinous sheath found in cyanobacteria primarily serves to:
Protect the filament and retain moisture
The gelatinous sheath around cyanobacterial filaments provides protection and helps retain moisture.
Antibiotics such as streptomycin are produced with the help of:
Many antibiotics, including streptomycin, are produced using heterotrophic bacteria.
Rhizobium, a nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in legume root nodules, is an example of:
Rhizobium is a heterotrophic bacterium that fixes nitrogen symbiotically in the root nodules of leguminous plants.
Which structure allows some bacteria to survive unfavourable conditions?
Bacteria form resistant spores to survive unfavourable environmental conditions.
The rigid cell wall in Eubacteria, combined with a flagellum (if motile), allows them to be classified as:
Eubacteria (true bacteria) have a rigid cell wall and, if motile, a flagellum.
Golden algae (desmids) belong to which protist group?
Chrysophytes include diatoms and desmids (golden algae), both largely photosynthetic planktonic protists.
Euglenoids are typically found in which habitat?
Euglenoids are mostly found in fresh, stagnant water bodies.
Which pigments found in Euglenoids resemble those in higher plants?
Photosynthetic pigments similar to higher plants
Euglenoids have pigments similar to those found in higher plants, supporting their photosynthetic ability in light.
The favourable-condition stage of slime moulds that can grow and spread over surfaces is called the:
Under favourable conditions, slime moulds form a plasmodium that can grow and spread over decaying matter.
A wall made of chitin only
Slime mould spores have true, resistant walls, aiding their survival and dispersal via air currents.
Which protozoan group includes free-living as well as parasitic forms with flagella for locomotion?
Flagellated protozoans include both free-living and parasitic forms, such as Trypanosoma.
Leishmania, a flagellated protozoan, causes kala-azar.
Some marine amoeboid protozoans possess protective shells made of:
Certain marine amoeboid forms secrete silica shells for protection.
Which structure in ciliated protozoans sweeps food-laden water into a specific cavity?
In ciliated protozoans like Paramoecium, coordinated cilia move water with food particles into a gullet cavity.
Sporozoans are characterised by having an infectious stage in their life cycle that is:
Sporozoans, like Plasmodium, have a spore-like infective stage in their life cycle.
Septate hyphae, as opposed to coenocytic hyphae, are characterised by the presence of:
Septate hyphae have cross walls (septa) dividing the hypha into cells, unlike coenocytic (aseptate) hyphae.
Vegetative reproduction in fungi occurs mainly by:
Vegetative reproduction in fungi includes fragmentation, fission, and budding.
Conidia, sporangiospores, and zoospores are all types of:
Conidia, sporangiospores, and zoospores are asexual spores produced by fungi.
Oospores, ascospores, and basidiospores are all types of:
Oospores, ascospores, and basidiospores are sexual spores resulting from fungal sexual reproduction.
In Phycomycetes, sexual reproduction may occur through fusion of gametes that are:
Phycomycetes show varied gamete fusion types — isogamous, anisogamous, or oogamous — forming a thick-walled zygospore.
Neurospora, often used in genetic research, belongs to which fungal class?
Neurospora, a model organism in genetics, is an Ascomycete fungus.
Claviceps, associated with ergot of rye, belongs to which fungal class?
Claviceps, the causal agent of ergot disease in rye, is classified under Ascomycetes.
Ustilago, the causative agent of smut disease, belongs to which fungal class?
Ustilago (smut) is a Basidiomycete fungus, along with Agaricus (mushroom) and Puccinia (rust).
Agaricus, the common mushroom, belongs to which fungal class?
Trichoderma, useful in biocontrol, belongs to which fungal class?
Trichoderma is a Deuteromycete fungus, valued for its biocontrol properties against plant pathogens.
Mucor, a common bread mould, belongs to which fungal class?
Mucor, along with Rhizopus, is a classic example of Phycomycetes with aseptate, coenocytic mycelium.
Albugo, causing white rust disease in plants, belongs to which fungal class?
Albugo, causing white rust of crucifers, belongs to Phycomycetes.
Deuteromycetes play an important ecological role by helping in:
Deuteromycetes help in mineral cycling as important decomposers, alongside their pathogenic roles in some species.
Which fungal class typically lacks any known asexual spore stage?
Basidiomycetes lack asexual spores; their vegetative reproduction is mainly by fragmentation.
Which structure bears the conidiophores in Ascomycetes?
In Ascomycetes, conidia are produced exogenously on specialised hyphae called conidiophores.
Plant cell walls are made primarily of:
Plant cell walls are composed of cellulose, distinguishing them from fungal (chitin) walls.
Sarracenia, another insectivorous plant besides Venus flytrap, is commonly known as the:
Sarracenia is a type of pitcher plant, an insectivorous plant that traps insects.
Drosera, an insectivorous plant, is commonly known as:
Drosera, commonly called sundew, is an insectivorous plant with sticky glandular hairs.
Sexual reproduction in Kingdom Animalia typically occurs via copulation of male and female followed by:
In animals, sexual reproduction by copulation is followed by embryological development of the offspring.
Which of the five plant divisions represents the most primitive, non-vascular land plants?
Bryophyta represents primitive, non-vascular land plants among the five divisions of Kingdom Plantae.
Which scientist showed that virus-infected plant extract, when applied to healthy plants, causes disease?
Beijerinck (1898) demonstrated that the infectious extract from diseased plants could cause disease in healthy plants.
The nucleoprotein nature of viruses refers to the fact that they are made of:
A virus, being a nucleoprotein, is composed of nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) surrounded by protein.
Which arrangement of capsomeres is common in the viral capsid?
Capsomeres in a viral capsid are commonly arranged in helical or polyhedral (icosahedral) patterns.
Which plant disease symptom is commonly caused by viral infection?
Viral infections in plants commonly cause symptoms like mosaic patterns, leaf yellowing, and vein clearing.
Chrysanthemum stunt disease is caused by a:
Chrysanthemum stunt disease is caused by a viroid, similar to potato spindle tuber disease.
Which vector transmits potato spindle tuber viroid (PSTVD)?
PSTVD is transmitted by aphids among potato plants.
Prions are unusual infectious agents because they:
Contain no nucleic acid, only misfolded protein
Contain a protein coat around DNA
Prions are unique in being infectious agents composed solely of misfolded protein, without any nucleic acid.
Lichens growing abundantly in an area typically indicate:
Since lichens fail to grow in polluted air, their abundance indicates relatively clean, unpolluted air.
In a lichen, which partner is responsible for absorbing water and minerals?
The fungal partner (mycobiont) absorbs water and minerals and provides shelter, while the phycobiont photosynthesises.
The fungal partners in a lichen are typically drawn from which two fungal classes?
Lichen-forming fungi are typically drawn from Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.
Which classification best fits an organism that is prokaryotic, unicellular, and photosynthetic using chlorophyll a?
Such an organism is a cyanobacterium, placed in Kingdom Monera due to its prokaryotic nature.
Which characteristic is shared by both Kingdom Fungi and Kingdom Animalia?
Both Fungi and Animalia show heterotrophic nutrition, though through different mechanisms (absorption vs ingestion).
Which structure in fungi is responsible for anchoring and nutrient absorption from the substrate?
The mycelium (network of hyphae) anchors the fungus and absorbs nutrients from the substrate.
Bacteria that are autotrophic and photosynthetic, using CO2 and H2O, are best exemplified by:
Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophic bacteria, using CO2 and H2O like green plants.
Which structure allows Euglenoids to be flexible in shape, unlike organisms with rigid cell walls?
The flexible, protein-rich pellicle allows Euglenoids to change shape, unlike rigid-walled organisms.
Which of these is true about the cell wall of Kingdom Animalia members?
Animal cells lack a cell wall entirely, unlike plant, fungal, or bacterial cells.
Fungal reproduction that requires the fusion of compatible hyphae, sometimes producing a dikaryotic stage, is termed:
Sexual reproduction in fungi involves fusion of compatible hyphae, sometimes with an intervening dikaryotic (n+n) stage.
Which is the correct sequence of increasing structural complexity across Whittaker's five kingdoms as conventionally presented?
The conventional order Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia reflects increasing complexity in cell and body organisation.
Which best describes the relationship between fungi and the roots of higher plants in mycorrhiza?
Mutualistic, benefiting both fungus and plant
Mycorrhiza is generally a mutualistic association benefiting both the fungus and the host plant's nutrient uptake.
Which is a defining feature separating Kingdom Monera from all other kingdoms?
The absence of a nuclear membrane (prokaryotic organisation) uniquely defines Kingdom Monera among the five kingdoms.
If a fungus is found to reproduce only by conidia with no known sexual phase, it would provisionally be classified under:
Fungi lacking a known sexual phase and reproducing only by asexual conidia are classified as Deuteromycetes (fungi imperfecti) until a sexual stage is found.
A dairy scientist notices that milk left uncovered turns into curd. Which group of organisms is most directly responsible?
Heterotrophic bacteria are responsible for converting milk to curd, among other decomposer roles.
Which feature would you check first to distinguish a virus from a viroid in the lab?
Viruses have a protein coat (capsid); viroids lack one and exist as free RNA — this is the key distinguishing feature.
A lichen is transplanted from a rural forest to a busy city centre and dies within weeks. This best illustrates that lichens:
Are sensitive indicators of air pollution
Lichens are well known as bioindicators of air pollution since they fail to grow/survive in polluted environments.
An organism shows alternation of generation between a diploid and haploid phase and has a cellulosic cell wall with chloroplasts. It belongs to:
Alternation of generation, cellulose cell wall, and chloroplasts are hallmark features of Kingdom Plantae.
A soil sample contains an organism with coenocytic, aseptate mycelium and forms zygospores. It most likely belongs to:
Aseptate, coenocytic mycelium and zygospore formation are characteristic of Phycomycetes like Rhizopus and Mucor.
If a fungus shows a dikaryotic (n+n) stage before karyogamy, which class(es) is it most likely to belong to?
The dikaryophase is characteristic mainly of Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes.
A plant shows partial heterotrophy by trapping and digesting insects, yet still photosynthesises. Which kingdom does it belong to?
Insectivorous plants like Dionaea remain in Kingdom Plantae despite partial heterotrophy, since they are still photosynthetic autotrophs primarily.
Which observation would best support classifying an unknown microbe under Kingdom Monera rather than Protista?
Absence of a nuclear membrane (prokaryotic organisation) places an organism in Monera, whereas Protista members have well-defined nuclei.
Why are diatoms considered ecologically vital despite being microscopic?
They are the chief producers of the ocean
Diatoms are the chief primary producers of oceanic ecosystems, forming the base of marine food chains.
A fungus is found growing symbiotically on tree bark along with a green alga, forming a crust-like structure. This structure is best identified as a:
A fungus-alga symbiotic association forming crust-like or leaf-like growths on surfaces like bark is a lichen.
A microbe is found in a bovine rumen, is strictly anaerobic, and releases methane gas as a metabolic byproduct. This organism belongs to which group?
Methane production in anaerobic gut environments is characteristic of methanogenic Archaebacteria.
A student wants to distinguish a bacterium from a fungus in a mixed culture using only cell wall chemistry. Which test would be most informative?
Testing for presence of chitin vs peptidoglycan
Since bacterial walls are peptidoglycan and fungal walls are chitin-based, testing cell wall chemistry distinguishes the two directly.
A crop is found affected by rust-coloured pustules on leaves, and microscopy reveals basidiospores. The likely causal organism belongs to:
Rust disease with basidiospores is characteristic of Basidiomycetes, such as Puccinia.
A sample of pond water under a microscope shows an organism with a gullet, numerous cilia, and a defined shape. This organism is best classified as:
A gullet and numerous cilia are diagnostic features of ciliated protozoans like Paramoecium.
The two-kingdom system of classification (Plantae and Animalia) was proposed by:
Carolus Linnaeus proposed the two-kingdom system, classifying all living organisms into Plantae and Animalia.
Which criterion was NOT used by R.H. Whittaker while proposing the Five Kingdom Classification?
Whittaker's five kingdom system was based on cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships — not habitat.
Which of these organisms was placed in a separate kingdom, Protista, mainly because it did not fit into the plant-animal division?
Unicellular eukaryotes like Amoeba could not be clearly classified as plants or animals, leading to the creation of Kingdom Protista.
A group of organisms sharing common features and morphology which can interbreed and produce fertile offspring is called:
A species is a group of individuals with common features that are capable of interbreeding to produce fertile offspring.
The Five Kingdom system of classification was proposed in the year:
R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom classification in 1969.
Which kingdom in the Five Kingdom system includes only prokaryotic organisms?
Kingdom Monera includes only prokaryotic organisms such as bacteria, which lack a well-defined nucleus.
Bacteria having a rod shape are called:
Rod-shaped bacteria are called bacillus; spherical are coccus, comma-shaped are vibrio, and spiral are spirillum.
Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria mainly due to differences in their:
Archaebacteria have a distinct cell wall composition, which allows them to survive in extreme environments like hot springs and salty areas.
Heterocysts, the site of nitrogen fixation in cyanobacteria, are found in organisms such as:
Nostoc and Anabaena are cyanobacteria possessing specialised, thick-walled cells called heterocysts, which fix atmospheric nitrogen.
Bacteria that obtain nutrition through photosynthesis using bacteriochlorophyll are called:
Photosynthetic autotrophic bacteria contain bacteriochlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis in an anaerobic manner.
Diatoms belong to which group of protists?
Diatoms are chrysophytes with cell walls embedded with silica, forming indestructible "diatomaceous earth".
The organism that possesses characteristics of both plants and animals, having chlorophyll but also a gullet, is:
Euglena has chlorophyll (autotrophic in sunlight) but behaves heterotrophically in the absence of light, using a gullet-like structure.
Dinoflagellates that cause the phenomenon of 'red tide' in the sea are mostly:
Red dinoflagellates, when they multiply rapidly, may make the sea appear red, a phenomenon called 'red tide'.
Amoeba, Paramecium and Plasmodium are grouped under which protist group?
Protozoans are heterotrophic protists including Amoeba, Paramecium, and the parasitic Plasmodium.
The vegetative body of a fungus is made up of long, slender thread-like structures called:
The fungal body consists of thread-like hyphae, and a network of hyphae is called a mycelium.
Sexual spores found in Ascomycetes (sac fungi) are called:
Ascomycetes produce endogenously formed sexual spores called ascospores, contained within a sac-like ascus.
In the fungal sexual cycle, the fusion of two haploid nuclei to form a diploid zygote nucleus is termed:
Karyogamy is the fusion of two haploid nuclei following plasmogamy, forming a diploid zygote nucleus.
Yeast, used in baking and brewing, belongs to which class of fungi?
Yeast (Saccharomyces) is an Ascomycete widely used in baking and brewing industries.
Arrange the three main steps of the fungal sexual cycle in correct order:
The fungal sexual cycle proceeds: Plasmogamy (fusion of protoplasms) → Karyogamy (fusion of nuclei) → Meiosis (formation of haploid spores).
Insectivorous plants like Nepenthes and Drosera are considered partially heterotrophic because they:
Trap and digest insects to supplement nutrition
Insectivorous plants photosynthesise but also trap and digest insects, supplementing nutrition, especially nitrogen.
Depend directly or indirectly on plants for food
Animals cannot synthesise their own food and depend directly or indirectly on plants, making them heterotrophic.
Viruses are described as obligate parasites because they:
Can multiply only inside a living host cell
Viruses lack their own metabolic machinery and can replicate only inside a living host cell, making them obligate parasites.
The protein coat surrounding the genetic material of a virus is called:
The capsid is the protein coat made of small subunits called capsomeres that encloses the viral genetic material.
T.O. Diener discovered which infectious agent smaller than viruses?
T.O. Diener discovered viroids, infectious agents even smaller than viruses, consisting of free RNA.
Arrange in order of increasing structural complexity: Viroid, Virus, Prion (in terms of possessing both nucleic acid and protein coat):
Prion has neither nucleic acid nor a coat (protein only); Viroid has RNA but no coat; Virus has both nucleic acid and a protein coat.
A lichen is a symbiotic association between:
A lichen is a symbiotic association between an alga (phycobiont) and a fungus (mycobiont).
In a lichen association, the alga (phycobiont) is responsible for:
Absorbing water and minerals, providing shelter
The phycobiont (algal partner) is autotrophic and photosynthetic, preparing food for the lichen association.
Lichens play an important ecological role as pioneers in:
Lichens are often pioneer organisms in plant succession, colonising bare rocks before other plants can grow.
Aristotle's habitat-based grouping of animals divided them into:
Besides the Enaima/Anaima division by blood colour, Aristotle also grouped animals by habitat into Aquatic and Terrestrial forms.
Linnaeus's Two Kingdom system placed fungi under the kingdom:
In the two-kingdom system, all non-green, non-motile organisms including fungi were grouped under Plantae, since the system used only two kingdoms.
In the Five Kingdom Classification, which characteristic was used to separate Monera from all other kingdoms?
Monera is the only kingdom of prokaryotes; all other four kingdoms (Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) consist of eukaryotic organisms.
Cyanobacteria are also commonly known as:
Cyanobacteria (e.g., Nostoc, Anabaena) are photosynthetic prokaryotes commonly called blue-green algae.
The fungal class characterised by the presence of coenocytic (aseptate) mycelium is:
Phycomycetes (e.g., Mucor, Rhizopus) have aseptate, coenocytic mycelium.
Movement of materials within the plant body occurs through vascular tissues, whereas in animals it occurs mainly through the:
Animals possess a circulatory system (blood/lymph) for internal transport, unlike plants which use vascular tissues (xylem and phloem).
The scientist who first crystallised the Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) and showed it to be largely protein was:
W.M. Stanley (1935) showed that viruses could be crystallised and that the crystals consist largely of protein.
In the association forming a lichen, the fungal component (mycobiont) belongs mainly to:
The mycobiont in lichens is generally a member of Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.
